steps.name: conductor_area
steps.formula: A = I sqrt(t) / k x (1 + corrosion allowance)

inputs.name: k
inputs.source: IS 3043 adiabatic sizing A = I sqrt(t) / k, k = 80 for GI, as quoted in J. Parmar, 'How to determine correct number of earthing electrodes, part 2', electrical-engineering-portal.com

steps.source: IS 3043 adiabatic sizing A = I sqrt(t) / k, k = 80 for GI, as quoted in J. Parmar, 'How to determine correct number of earthing electrodes, part 2', electrical-engineering-portal.com

steps.name: ieee80_area

inputs.name: Kf
inputs.source: IEEE Std 80 simplified sizing A_kcmil = I_kA Kf sqrt(tc), Kf = 28.96 for zinc-coated steel (Tm 419 C, Ta 40 C), A_kcmil = 1.974 A_mm2; IEEE 80 table as reproduced in 'Electrical Safety Practice and Standards', Table 8.3

steps.source: IEEE Std 80 simplified sizing A_kcmil = I_kA Kf sqrt(tc), Kf = 28.96 for zinc-coated steel (Tm 419 C, Ta 40 C), A_kcmil = 1.974 A_mm2; IEEE 80 table as reproduced in 'Electrical Safety Practice and Standards', Table 8.3

steps.name: electrode_current
steps.formula: I = 7.57 x 1000 / sqrt(rho t) x pi d L
steps.source: IS 3043 maximum current density at the electrode surface J = 7.57 x 1000 / sqrt(rho t) A/m2, as quoted in J. Parmar, part 1, electrical-engineering-portal.com

steps.name: pipe_resistance
steps.formula: R = 100 rho / (2 pi L) ln(4 L / d), L and d in cm
steps.source: IS 3043 pipe or rod electrode R = 100 rho / (2 pi L) ln(4 L / d), L and d in cm, as quoted in J. Parmar, part 1, electrical-engineering-portal.com

steps.name: strip_resistance
steps.formula: R = 100 rho / (2 pi L) ln(2 L^2 / (w t)), L, w, t in cm
steps.source: IS 3043 buried strip R = 100 rho / (2 pi L) ln(2 L^2 / (w t)), L, w, t in cm, as quoted in J. Parmar, part 2, electrical-engineering-portal.com

assumptions: earth electrode 40 mm dia x 3 m long (as on the CIL/Refex earthing layout unless set)
pits spaced at least two electrode lengths apart are combined as parallel resistances, in parallel with the buried conductor
conductor sized to the larger of the IS 3043 (k = 80) and IEEE 80 (Kf = 28.96) cross-sections
no corrosion allowance on the conductor cross-section (set corrosion_allowance to add one)
25x3 GS flat down conductors (practice; confirm against IS/IEC 62305-3 and NF C 17-102 minimum sections)

target earth resistance 1 ohm (transformers and substation earthing below 1 ohm; earth resistance practice table in J. Parmar, 'How to determine correct number of earthing electrodes, part 2', electrical-engineering-portal.com); not a cited limit, set target_resistance_ohm to override
grid current taken as the full earth fault current (split factor 1, decrement factor 1; conservative)
flat strip 50x6 taken as a round conductor of diameter half its width in the IEEE 80 mesh equations
tolerable voltages for a 50 kg body
earth resistance taken as the larger of the pits-and-strip value and the Sverak (IEEE 80) value for the buried network over its convex hull
switchyard grid bonded to the plant earth network: ground potential rise from the combined earth resistance
ESE design to NF C 17-102, a French standard used in Indian EPC practice; IS/IEC 62305 does not recognise an enlarged ESE radius
